title: Probability-Entropy Calibration: An Elastic Indicator for Adaptive Fine-tuning
claim: Probability alone or entropy alone misjudges which tokens matter; jointly calibrating both separates truly under-learned tokens from noisy or replaceable ones.
layout: 2 panels: left token-indicator rows, right 2-D quadrant schematic with histogram insets
description: The left panel shows a ground-truth sentence ("The answer is, umm, essentially 5. 6") with circled numbers on key tokens. Below it are three rows of colored bars, one per indicator: GT probability p_t (with check and cross marks), token entropy H_t (labeled Replaceable or Noisy), and our Relative Rank I_t (labeled Negligible, Neutral or Prioritized, with stopwatch icons). Each indicator has a red-to-blue gradient arrow legend. The right panel is a (p_t, H_t) plane split into four quadrants by dash-dot lines. Each quadrant is numbered and has a small histogram inset with black GT bars and hatched prediction bars. The background gradient runs from red to teal, and a dashed circle at the top marks the Noise Region. The eye goes first to the colored bar rows, then to the quadrant schematic.
caption: A joint view of token correctness and intrinsic uncertainty. (Left) Token-level visualization of three indicators: the ground-truth probability $p_t$, token entropy $H_t$, and our Relative Rank Indicator $I_t$ (Sec. [ref]). Colors encode relative magnitude; arrows indicate the increasing direction. (Right) A schematic in the $(p_t,H_t)$ plane with four regimes (\circled{1}--\circled{4}) distinguished by $I_t$; the background color gradient encodes $I_t$ values; inset histograms show representative predictive distributions for typical tokens (e.g., "essentially", "is", "5", "6"); the dashed circle marks a Noise Region (\circled{5}).
abstract: Token-level reweighting is a simple yet effective mechanism for controlling supervised fine-tuning, but common indicators are largely one-dimensional: the ground-truth probability reflects downstream alignment, while token entropy reflects intrinsic uncertainty induced by the pre-training prior. Ignoring entropy can misidentify noisy or easily replaceable tokens as learning-critical, while ignoring probability fails to reflect target-specific alignment. RankTuner introduces a probability--entropy calibration signal, the Relative Rank Indicator, which compares the rank of the ground-truth token with its expected rank under the prediction distribution. The inverse indicator is used as a token-wise Relative Scale to reweight the fine-tuning objective, focusing updates on truly under-learned tokens without over-penalizing intrinsically uncertain positions. Experiments on multiple backbones show consistent improvements on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, transfer gains on out-of-distribution reasoning, and pre code generation performance over probability-only or entropy-only reweighting baselines.
